This run will be marked low confidence and will not be ranked.
How long one frame took. Lower is better, and it is what every number here is measured in.
The slowest 1% of frames. A driver can have a good average and still stutter, and this is where that shows.
Results are shown, but not ranked.

Ranking needs a separate calibration run first: the same driver against itself, which should show no difference at all. If it does show one, this device is manufacturing differences and no comparison on it can be trusted. That run has not been done here, so the comparison below is shown but kept out of any ranking. Nothing is wrong with the two drivers you chose.
The smallest difference this device can actually tell apart. Anything smaller is reported as a tie rather than a win.
The two drivers performed the same, as far as this device can measure. That is a real answer, not a failure.
The measurements were too scattered to conclude anything. Let the device cool down and run it again.
Results are only compared directly when they were measured in one sitting, from the same starting temperature.
This exact build is not in the app\'s catalogue. It still runs and still counts; it just cannot be given a known name.
The app asks Vulkan which driver actually answered, and refuses to run if it is not the one you chose.
No diagnostics have been recorded yet.
Logs are written to Android/data/%1$s/files/logs. Since Android 11 most file managers cannot open that folder, so use this button.
This device has never been calibrated, so results will be shown without a ranking.
Calibration failed on this device. Results are still measured, but nothing is ranked.
The stored calibration does not cover the workloads in the selected profile, so this profile cannot be ranked.

The app runs one driver against itself and expects to find no difference. Any difference it does find was manufactured by this device — thermal drift, clock steps, background load — and sets the limit on what a real comparison can claim. Until that limit is known, results are shown but never ranked.

Eight comparisons at fifteen runs per arm, on the workloads of the selected profile — around two hours. There is no shorter honest version. Fewer runs per arm does not measure the device, it measures the sample size: at five, the interval around a difference is about 20%% wide however steady the hardware is. Keep the device unplugged, cool and idle.
This device resolves differences of about %1$s or larger on %2$s.
The resolution of this device is not known yet: no A/A comparison has completed on it.
This stops as soon as the result is decided, which is usually long before the last execution.

Measures whether this device is unsteady inside a run or between runs. It quadruples the frame count on half the comparisons and compares the spread. If the spread halves, longer runs buy precision far more cheaply than more runs. It produces no calibration: share the diagnostics afterwards.

Measures whether the 20 s wait between arms — about 70% of this run\u2019s wall time — is doing anything. It halves that wait on half the comparisons and compares the results. It produces no calibration: share the diagnostics afterwards.
